title: Stop Funding the Emergency. Start Financing Inclusion.
author: Elizabeth Campbell
authorBio: Elizabeth Campbell is the founding executive director of CoAction Global, a nonprofit impact accelerator. Her career spans government, civil society and the United Nations, with a focus on multilateralism, diplomacy and humanitarian action.
pullQuote: Refugee displacement is long-term, so financing solutions must be too.
standfirst: Protracted displacement cannot be financed as a recurring emergency. A new model would tie long-term finance to inclusion reforms and give refugees direct capital.
imageAlt: Stop Funding the Emergency. Start Financing Inclusion. - Displacement Policy Perspectives preview card

title: States are the Solution, Not the Problem
author: Peter De Clercq
authorRole: Former UN Assistant Secretary-General · Adjunct Professor, Nelson Mandela University
authorBio: Peter De Clercq has held senior United Nations leadership roles across humanitarian, development and peacebuilding contexts.
pullQuote: Sustainable protection in displacement contexts must be anchored in national systems and the rule of law.
standfirst: Sustainable protection in displacement contexts must be anchored in national systems, local ownership, and the rule of law.
imageAlt: States are the Solution, Not the Problem - Displacement Policy Perspectives preview card

title: The System We Forgot We Were Building
author: Inah Kaloga
affiliation: Global Director, Violence Prevention & Response, IRC
authorRole: Global Director, Violence Prevention & Response, IRC
authorBio: Inah Kaloga leads global work on violence prevention and response at the International Rescue Committee.
pullQuote: The challenge now is not simply to deliver protection services, but to connect them more deliberately to the systems that sustain social change over time.
standfirst: Humanitarian protection and social work have always been more closely connected than the sector often admits.
imageAlt: The System We Forgot We Were Building - Displacement Policy Perspectives preview card

title: When Protection Leadership Is Not Enough
author: Samuel Cheung
authorBio: Samuel Cheung is Founder and Director of Displacement Policy and a former UNHCR protection official, including as Chief of Protection from Violence and Displacement and Global Protection Cluster Coordinator.
pullQuote: The reason is often not institutional weakness. It is institutional design.
standfirst: Protection leadership matters. But achieving protection outcomes also requires understanding the political and institutional systems through which change has to occur.
imageAlt: When Protection Leadership Is Not Enough - Displacement Policy Perspectives preview card

title: Humanitarian policy reform cannot substitute for displacement governance.
author: Samuel Cheung
authorBio: Samuel Cheung is Founder and Director of Displacement Policy and a former UNHCR protection official, including as Chief of Protection from Violence and Displacement and Global Protection Cluster Coordinator.
pullQuote: Humanitarian policy can name the governance gap. It cannot close it.
standfirst: After two decades of policy innovation, protection still often fails where institutional responsibility remains fragmented.
imageAlt: Humanitarian policy reform cannot substitute for displacement governance - Displacement Policy Perspectives preview card

title: The Problem No One Owns
author: Samuel Cheung
authorBio: Samuel Cheung is Founder and Director of Displacement Policy and a former UNHCR protection official, including as Chief of Protection from Violence and Displacement and Global Protection Cluster Coordinator.
pullQuote: The contemporary challenge is not only whether IDPs are recognized. It is whether responsibility for them is assigned, financed, and embedded.
standfirst: Internal displacement reveals what happens when protection needs are clear but responsibility remains fragmented.
